arxiv-1711-02427.title: The ACCompanion v0.1: An Expressive Accompaniment System
arxiv-1711-02427.description: Abstract In this paper we present a preliminary version of the ACCompanion, an expressive accompaniment system for MIDI input. The system uses a probabilistic monophonic score follower to track the position of the soloist in the score, and a linear Gaussian model to compute tempo updates.

arxiv-2004-08854.title: Planar Bichromatic Bottleneck Spanning Trees This work was partially supported by Grant 2016116 from the United States – Israel Binational Science Foundation. Mitchell was partially supported by NSF (CCF-1526406).
arxiv-2004-08854.creator: A. Karim Abu-Affash, Sujoy Bhore, Paz Carmi, Joseph S. B. Mitchell
arxiv-2004-08854.description: Abstract Given a set P P of n n red and blue points in the plane, a planar bichromatic spanning tree of P P is a spanning tree of P P , such that each edge connects between a red and a blue point, and no two edges intersect.

arxiv-2201-00493.title: Beauville-Voisin filtrations on zero cycles of moduli space of stable sheaves on K3 surfaces
arxiv-2201-00493.creator: Zhiyuan Li, Ruxuan Zhang
arxiv-2201-00493.description: Abstract . The Beauville-Voisin conjecture predicts the existence of a filtration on projective hyper-Kähler manifolds opposite to the conjecture Bloch-Beilinson filtration, called the Beauivlle-Voisin filtration. In [ Voi16 ] , Voisin has introduced a filtration on zero cycles of an arbitrary projective hyper-Kähler manifold.

arxiv-2202-09592.title: Nuclear quantum effects on the vibrational dynamics of the water-air interface
arxiv-2202-09592.creator: Deepak Ojha, Andrés Henao, Frederik Zysk, Thomas D. Kühne
arxiv-2202-09592.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Deepak Ojha, Andrés Henao, Frederik Zysk, Thomas D. Kühne. We have applied path integral molecular dynamics simulations to investigate nuclear quantum effects on the vibrational dynamics of water molecules at the water-air interface. The instantaneous fluctuations in the frequencies of the O-H stretch modes are calculated using the wavelet method of time series analysis, while the time scales of vibrational spectral diffusion are determined from frequency-time correlation functions and joint probability distributions, as well as the hydrogen bond number correlation functions.

arxiv-2307-06009.title: A Linear Algebraic Framework for Dynamic Scheduling Over Memory-Equipped Quantum Networks
arxiv-2307-06009.creator: PAOLO FITTIPALDI 1, ANASTASIOS GIOVANIDIS 1,2 , AND FRÉDÉRIC GROSSHANS 1
arxiv-2307-06009.description: Abstract Quantum Internetworking is a recent field that promises numerous interesting applications, many of which require the distribution of entanglement between arbitrary pairs of users. This work deals with the problem of scheduling in an arbitrary entanglement swapping quantum network — often called first generation quantum network — in its general topology, multicommodity, loss-aware formulation.

arxiv-2507-18286.title: Unconventional Thermalization of a Localized Chain Interacting with an Ergodic Bath
arxiv-2507-18286.creator: Konrad Pawlik, Nicolas Laflorencie, Jakub Zakrzewski
arxiv-2507-18286.description: Abstract The study of many-body localized (MBL) phases intrinsically links spectral properties with eigenstate characteristics: localized systems exhibit Poisson level statistics and area-law entanglement entropy, while ergodic systems display volume-law entanglement and follow random matrix theory predictions, including level repulsion. Here, we introduce the interacting Anderson Quantum Sun model, which significantly deviates from these conventional expectations.

arxiv-2511-09443.title: BronchOpt : Vision-Based Pose Optimization with Fine-Tuned Foundation Models for Accurate Bronchoscopy Navigation
arxiv-2511-09443.creator: Hongchao Shu, Roger D. Soberanis-Mukul, Jiru Xu, Hao Ding, Morgan Ringel, Mali Shen, Saif Iftekar Sayed, Hedyeh Rafii-Tari, Mathias Unberath
arxiv-2511-09443.description: Abstract Purpose: Accurate intra-operative localization of the endoscope tip relative to the anatomy remains a major challenge in bronchoscopy due to respiratory motion, anatomical variability, and CT-to-body divergence, which cause deformation and misalignment between intra-operative views and pre-operative CT. Existing vision-based methods often struggle generalize across domains and patients, limiting robustness and leaving residual alignment errors.

Here, we report deep learning...

pmc-10670886.title: A Systematic Review of In Vitro Studies Using Microchip Platforms for Identifying Periodontopathogens from the Red Complex
pmc-10670886.creator: Carlos M Ardila, Gustavo A Jiménez-Arbeláez, Annie Marcela Vivares-Builes, Patrick R Schmidlin
pmc-10670886.description: Porphyromonas gingivalis, Tannerella forsythia, and Treponema denticola, collectively recognized as periodontopathogens within the red complex, have been extensively studied in clinical samples collected from individuals with periodontitis. A lab-on-a-chip (LOC) is a miniature mechanism that integrates various laboratory operations onto a single microchip or a small-scale platform.

pmc-10674103.title: The impact of perioperative non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs use on pleurodesis following thoracic surgery
pmc-10674103.creator: Kudzayi Kutywayo, Akolade A Habib, Edward J Caruana
pmc-10674103.description: SummaryA best evidence topic in thoracic surgery was written according to a structured protocol. The question addressed was: in patients who have had {visceral and parietal pleural symphysis}, {do NSAIDs reduce} {the efficacy of pleurodesis}? Sixteen papers were discovered in the search. Of these, 3 human studies were included in the analysis.

pmc-10753662.title: Bilateral Hoffa Fractures of the Medial Femoral Condyles: A Case Report and Review of the Literature
pmc-10753662.creator: Antonios Kouzelis, Evangelia Argyropoulou, Balasis Stavros, Spyridon Papagiannis, Panagiotis Antzoulas, John Gliatis
pmc-10753662.description: Introduction:Intra-articular distal femoral fractures in the coronal plane, widely described as Hoffa fractures, are a rare entity. Lateral femoral condyles are mostly affected, while diagnosis can be challenging. Bilateral medial femoral condyle fractures are exceedingly scarce, with only one case being published in recent literature.

pmc-11541446.title: Design and Optimization of a Chemical Looping Hydrogen Production System Using Steam Reforming for Petrochemical Plants
pmc-11541446.creator: Mohammad Saeedan, Ehsan Houshfar
pmc-11541446.description: Industrial pollution is a significant environmental concern, and researchers are seeking solutions to minimize its impact. Chemical looping combustion is an efficient technique to decrease CO2 emissions. This study delves into its application within petrochemical plants for hydrogen production. In addition to its high efficiency in hydrogen production, this method yields pure CO2 and nitrogen.

pmc-11607768.title: Visceral adiposity as a predictor of new-onset diabetes in patients with primary aldosteronism: a cohort study
pmc-11607768.creator: Wen-Kai Chu, Leay Kiaw Er, Chin-Chen Chang, Jin-Ying Lu, Wan-Chen Wu, Yao-Chou Tsai, Yen-Hung Lin, Vin-Cent Wu
pmc-11607768.description: Background:Patients with primary aldosteronism (PA) exhibit a high prevalence of diabetes mellitus (DM). However, the relationship between visceral adipose tissue (VAT) and new-onset diabetes mellitus (NODM) in PA patients remains unclear.Objectives:To explore the association between VAT and the risk of NODM in PA patients.Design:This is a prospective cohort study spanning 10 years (2010–2020).

pmc-12592430.title: SERPINA1 gene regulates the tumorigenesis and progression of breast cancer through PI3K/AKT signaling pathway and tumor immune microenvironment
pmc-12592430.creator: Chuqi Lei, Wei Lu, Yuan Li, Huaiyu yang, Ke Zhang, Nianchang Wang, Lixue Xuan, Changyuan Guo
pmc-12592430.description: This study aims to reveal the influence of SERPINA1 gene on the development, prognosis evaluation and immune environment changes of breast cancer. Cell lines with differential SERPINA1 expression were constructed. These models were used to explore its impact on the biological behavior of breast cancer cells.

pmc-12612699.title: The social origins of consciousness
pmc-12612699.creator: Kristin Andrews, Noam Miller
pmc-12612699.description: We present the social origins of consciousness hypothesis, according to which the ability to coordinate with group members was the original adaptive function of consciousness. We offer three arguments. The phylogenetic argument presumes that consciousness is widespread among existing animals, and that widespread capacities are probably evolutionarily old.

pmc-12729445.title: Clinical Profile, Endoscopic Findings, and Outcomes Among Inpatients With Upper Gastrointestinal Bleeding in a United Kingdom District General Hospital
pmc-12729445.creator: Mansur F Mohammed, Rajesh K Gurunathan, Nourhan N Eltanikhy, Pavithra Dhanasekaran
pmc-12729445.description: BackgroundAcute upper gastrointestinal bleeding (AUGIB) is a medical emergency associated with significant morbidity and mortality. Prognosis and management are typically determined by the patient’s clinical features and findings on endoscopy.ObjectiveThis study aimed to evaluate the demographic characteristics, risk stratification, endoscopic findings, and therapeutic interventions in patients presenting with AUGIB at Queens Hospital, Burton, United Kingdom, in 2024.

pmc-13130912.title: Safety and Feasibility of Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement in Patients With Hematologic Neoplasms
pmc-13130912.creator: Nicholas W. Prinz, Joshua Thomas, Mevin A. Mathew, Jeet J. Mehta, Bibhu D. Mohanty
pmc-13130912.description: For patients with severe, symptomatic aortic stenosis (AS) who are poor surgical candidates, transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) offers a less invasive alternative to surgical valve replacement. Patients with hematologic neoplasms and severe AS are a high-risk subset, with increased risk of bleeding and infection, who have historically been excluded from clinical investigation in TAVR.

pmc-13156361.title: Unveiling Hepatic Protein Alterations in Neonatal and Infant Biliary Atresia
pmc-13156361.creator: Zubida M Al‐Majdoub, Martyn Howard, Brahim Achour, Jill Barber, Naved Alizai, Amin Rostami‐Hodjegan
pmc-13156361.description: Pediatric populations differ from adults in drug elimination capacity. While current scaling methods account for enzyme and transporter maturation, they overlook comorbidities, such as biliary atresia (BA), a liver disease appearing within the first 2–8 weeks of life that can progress to cirrhosis. Such conditions may impair hepatic drug clearance, requiring dose adjustments.

pmc-13241993.title: Prolonged Dysesthesia After Massive Accidental Semaglutide Overdose: A Case Report
pmc-13241993.creator: Massimo Quarenghi, Anastasia Stanga, Alessia Bergamaschi
pmc-13241993.description: The use of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) has expanded rapidly worldwide for the treatment of obesity, accompanied by a parallel increase in medication errors and accidental overdoses. Gastrointestinal symptoms are the most commonly reported adverse effects in cases of supratherapeutic exposure, whereas neurologic manifestations remain poorly characterized.

pmc-13318000.title: Seen but not heard: A qualitative interview study exploring the views and experiences of children and young people referred to Child and Adolescent Mental Health Services for support with suicidality
pmc-13318000.creator: Lynne Gilmour, Margaret Maxwell, Edward Duncan
pmc-13318000.description: Suicide is a leading cause of death amongst children and young people (CYP), and numbers of CYP presenting with suicidality continue to rise. CYP seeking help for suicidal thoughts and behaviours are generally referred to Child and Adolescent Mental Health Services (CAMHS) for assessment and treatment. However, CAMHS across the UK are unable to meet the demand for their services.

pmc-13511535.title: A Multi-Model Strategy for Optimizing Hepatitis B Virus preS1 Epitope Recognition by the Antibody HzKR127
pmc-13511535.creator: Wenqing Chen, Yuanzhong Tu, Kai Wang, Runze Xie, Pengyuan Yang, Yanan Gao, Wenxiang Huang
pmc-13511535.description: Functional cure of chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection remains a significant challenge, making viral-entry-blocking antibodies a promising antiviral strategy. Here, we developed a structure-guided computational workflow for affinity-enhancing candidate mutations at the interface between the humanized neutralizing antibody HzKR127 and the HBV preS1 peptide epitope.
